JCM906 identifies a separately sterilized 0.5 M glycine-NaOH buffer at pH 10.0. This defines a stock preparation even though its solvent and the amount of NaOH are not stated. The source specifies 100 mL of stock; the frozen 100 G_PER_L receiving dose is a separate normalization defect.

The TOGO M2844 comment identifies a 0.5% bromothymol blue solution in 0.2 N KOH, added at 5 mL per litre. A stock owner can preserve this combined preparation. The extracted 0.2NKOH fragment must not denote the whole stock or be added as a global alias.

JCM600 identifies an anaerobic, autoclaved water-saturated toluene stock described as 5.0 mM and added at 40 mL per litre. This supports a stock record separate from pure toluene and from the receiving medium.
NBRC19 names Peptic Pepton from USB at 2 g/L. The named commercial material can have an opaque product record without an invented substrate, digestion process or catalog number.

DSMZ88 permits sulfide ore and gives pyrite as an example for DSM5348. The source denotes a generic ore material rather than pure FeS2 or a fixed mineral mixture. A registry record preserves that unspecified material without requiring a mineral assay.

The existing Cereal_Leaves record denotes cereal leaf tissue of unspecified species, matching the material named in the CCAP recipes. Promote this existing material to a registry identity and preserve the supplier and preparation context without asserting a plant species or extract composition.

The frozen MediaDive1938 occurrence explicitly describes a 0.5 M HOMOPIPES preparation at pH 5.4, dosed by volume. The existing CAS owner identifies the solute. A separate stock record can assert the named solute and concentration while leaving the vehicle and titrant unspecified.

The source explicitly specifies DL-asparagine with one water. Wako identifies DL-asparagine monohydrate as CAS 69833-18-7. TCI uses 3130-87-8 for a hydrate product, but that number also appears on generic asparagine records; it is not copied. A distinct CAS 69833-18-7 owner retains a broad relation to CHEBI:22653 asparagine.

CHEBI:6364 and CAS 9008-22-4 denote laminarin across brown-algal taxa. The current owner has this generic identity but a Laminaria digitata procurement label. Align its preferred name to Laminarin and preserve the original species detail in supplied_form and a catalog synonym. No evidence supports a distinct chemical substance requiring a second owner.

Source-supported material or preparation identity under MAPPING_SEMANTICS sections 3 and 6. Bounded ontology and catalog searches found no verified exact term for this scope. No component identity is assigned to the whole preparation.

The three FEBA recipes use unqualified R2A at one-fold strength in liquid outgrowth media. MICRO:0000541 supplies the named R2A-medium concept, while MICRO:0000543 separately denotes R2A agar. A generic named-medium record can preserve this source sense without inventing a supplier or formula.

The primary TOGO M2972 component is explicitly labelled Difco R2A agar, and the preparation describes plant-stem contact with a medium surface. This supports the agar interpretation of this occurrence and a source-provenance enrichment of the existing R2A-agar owner.

The preparation is a racemic sodium-salt form of the generic acid. This is an asymmetric parent anchor, not chemical identity; the source-defined preparation keeps its own registry identity. The full Denger2010 methods identify 10 mM racemic sulfolactate and explicitly cite the Roy2003 synthesis. Roy identifies the synthesized material as sodium sulfolactate. The chain supports a source-defined racemic sodium-sulfolactate preparation; sodium stoichiometry, hydration and isolated-product purity remain unspecified.

MICRO:0000113 explicitly includes Trypticase soy broth and describes the standard BBL formulation: casein digest, soybean digest, dextrose, NaCl and dipotassium phosphate. Promote the existing generic Trypticase-soy-broth owner, retaining its history and counts. The NBRC source uses 30 g of this base with agar supplied separately.

The current owner mixes concentration labels and an L-specific label into the alias channel of sodium lactate. Retype the 1 M stock, 1% stock and L-only label as rejected provenance, retaining their original text and source. The DL salt name and existing identifier remain unchanged; this repairs concrete alias defects without approving the withheld row.

FOODON:00004510 denotes flour as a powder from cereals or other starchy sources. This generic material sense matches the unqualified plain-flour ingredient; an identified grain is not required to preserve it. Promote the existing owner to the flour term without assigning wheat, bleaching, fortification or an automatic CAS cross-reference.
